consensus_summary: Primary meaning across responses is right standing before God (especially forensic/imputed righteousness credited by faith in Christ, apart from works) together with conformity to God’s moral character and standards; frequent garment/robe symbolism; common alternatives are infused/transformative righteousness, ethical conduct, covenant faithfulness, God’s own saving justice, social justice, and Christ as righteousness itself.
book_summary: The doing of God’s commandments—the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts; not a vague goodness nor a verdict only received.
consensus_core_identification: Right standing with God (status/gift, often imputed) plus ethical conformity to His will/character.
book_core_identification: Active doing/keeping of God’s commandments and righteous acts (as garment).
boundary_disagreement: Book excludes pure forensic/imputed cases of a verdict merely received by faith and requires actual observance of commandments as constitutive; consensus primary admits status alone (or status primary) as righteousness.
material_contradiction: None at the shared ethical-conformity core; the book only rejects the sufficiency of ‘verdict only’ rather than denying every consensus element.
rationale: Minimum cores share the category of rightness relative to God/His law. Consensus primary joins status and conduct (with imputation dominant in the primary_meaning statements and notes); the book retains the conduct pole (already listed as common alternative and supported by overlapping bases such as 1 John 3:7 and the deeds-as-linen image) while materially narrowing extension and boundary conditions by insisting on ‘the law kept’ and by explicit denial of ‘a verdict only received.’ This is refinement of boundary/precision, not replacement of the central referent, hence REFINED rather than DIVERGENT or MATCH.
strongest_objection: Dominant Pauline texts (Rom 3–4; Phil 3:9; 2 Cor 5:21) treat righteousness as the gift of status in Christ apart from works of law, so the book’s rejection of ‘verdict only’ and exclusive focus on commandment-doing may invert the New-Testament priority while still citing only the behavioral texts.
